meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (federal level; cantonal registries administer incorporation)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU-Switzerland Free Trade Agreement of 22 July 1972
Switzerland-Hong Kong Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement of 2002
Double Taxation Agreements (DTAAs) with over 100 states, including Switzerland-China DTA of 1990 (amended 2013) and Switzerland-United States DTA of 1996 (amended by 2009 and 2019 protocols)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), Art. 697i-697l (beneficial owners register and bearer-share disclosure obligations), Art. 627-629 (registered seat and incorporation execution), Art. 632-637 (minimum capital and incorporation defects); Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0), Art. 2a, 3-8; Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0), Art. 305bis-305ter; FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (GwV-FINMA, SR 955.033.0) and FINMA Circular 2020/02; Swiss Embargo Act (SR 946.2) and implementing sanctions ordinances of the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO); Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Entities and the Identification of the Beneficial Owners (draft TLA, not yet in force).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of companies in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of 1961 for parties to the Convention; otherwise consular legalization by the competent Swiss representation abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the foreign corporate shareholder authorizing the incorporation of the Swiss Aktiengesellschaft and its key terms
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign shareholder company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as above; certified translation into German, French or Italian submitted to the Swiss notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original power of attorney of each founder for the incorporation step, with proof of identity annexed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founder or notary in the founder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; signatures to be verified by the Swiss notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport or ID card copy of every beneficial owner and board member, together with the beneficial-owner declaration under Art. 697j CO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent state identity authority or authorized certifying notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy; identity documents requiring legalization follow the Hague/consular path for non-member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or attestation evidencing actual deposit of at least CHF 50,000 of the subscribed capital on a Swiss bank account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss bank or financial intermediary licensed by FINMA
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required; original letter or authenticated SWIFT confirmation addressed to the Swiss notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory KYC before the notarial deed: each founder, beneficial owner and proxy is screened against Swiss domestic criminal records and sanctions lists under SECO (SR 946.2), UN Security Council resolutions, and EU measures taken over by Switzerland. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) trigger enhanced due diligence under AMLA Art. 2a and 3, GwV-FINMA (SR 955.033.0) and FINMA Circular 2020/02, requiring source-of-funds evidence and approval of senior management. For the intended Stripe/card-payment rails, matching against OFAC SDN is adopted as voluntary but prudent best practice. Suspicious activity reports shall be filed with MROS (Money Laundering Reporting Office Switzerland).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Official Swiss Commercial Register, operated cantonally and searchable through the federal ZEFIX portal (www.zefix.ch) and the Federal Office for Justice; the application is filed with the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (e.g., Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zurich). The registry's preliminary availability check has no legally binding reservation effect; only the completed entry creates name protection. The 30-day window in this dossier represents the standard statutory processing and review period within which the application, once filed, is examined before registration or refusal.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Latin characters and may be chosen in the official language of the canton of seat (German, French, Italian or Romansh); foreign words are tolerated if they identify the founder or the corporate purpose, but the name must not be deceptive or contrary to public order under Art. 950 CO. English terms are accepted in practice for technology firms if the name remains pronounceable and distinguishable; transliteration into the cantonal roman script is sufficient.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Swiss / Suisse / Svizzera / Schweizer (geographical indication protection)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The commercial registry performs an ex-ante rejection examination. On rejection, the applicant receives a written decision with grounds; it may either (i) file an administrative objection, or (ii) appeal within 30 days to the cantonal administrative or superior court, and finally to the Swiss Federal Court. A revised name may be re-filed at any time. The courts apply the principles for the protection of trade names (Art. 950-956 CO); names that are merely descriptive or liable to mislead are excluded.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual-office-only arrangements are not permissible as the registered seat. The AG must maintain an actual physical office in Switzerland that is fit for correspondence, meetings, archives and statutory records. Cantonal domiciliation providers may be used only where a complete workplace with document access infrastructure is made available to the client; a mere mailbox or forwarding service does not satisfy Art. 627 CO or the commercial registry practice.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (quantified residual risk: approximately 5% per year for a low-risk ISIC 3240 hardware manufacturing entity with no regulated activity and no trust or holding features). Unannounced inspections are lawful, but generally occur only on suspicion or as part of general anti-money-laundering reviews of registered-office and domiciliation companies.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Swiss legal counsel incorporation retainer, including review of existing group structure, UBO crossing, drafting of Articles of Association in German/French/Italian, and completion attendance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market lump-sum benchmark for a standard AG incorporation (CHF 4,000 for a simple single-shareholder deal)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial execution of the deed of incorporation (public deed witnessing the founders' meeting)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal Notarial Fee Schedule (CHF 500 notary fee for share capital up to CHF 250,000)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/CO), Art. 620 et seq. (Aktiengesellschaft); Arts. 629, 635, 638, 640, 698, 707, 712, 716a, 716b, 718, 725, 726, 731, 783
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), with subsequent publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certified deed of incorporation (Statuten/Acte constitutif) and application for registration in the Commercial Register (Handelsregister-Anmeldung)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital CHF 100,000 (approx. USD 110,000); at least 20% and in any event minimum CHF 50,000 (approx. USD 55,000) must be paid up in cash before registration, or replaced by a bank guarantee for the unpaid portion; capital must be deposited in a blocked Swiss escrow account and evidenced by a bank non-liability/blocking certificate until registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the founder-shareholders’ subscription of the 100,000 fully paid-up registered shares (nominal value CHF 1.00 each) is ratified, that the fully paid share capital is available for unrestricted corporate use, and that the corporate domicile at the principal place of business in the Canton of Zug is adopted. RESOLVED that Mr. Marc Berger and Ms. Elena Rossi are appointed as members of the Board of Directors with individual signatory authority, that Mr. Marc Berger is appointed as Chairperson, and that Ms. Nina Keller is appointed as the company’s registered office representative with power to complete the commercial register filing. RESOLVED that the Board is authorized to open bank accounts, engage the statutory auditor, and execute all required declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarisation of the Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canton of Zug Notary Public with authentication competence for company formations; reviewed by the Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Swiss notary licensed in Canton Zug. The founders must approve the deed of incorporation and articles of association in one sitting; the notary must certify the deed incorporating the corporate name (e.g., AI PET ROBOT AG), registered office in Zug, purpose covering development, assembly and distribution of interactive robotic companion animals with speech synthesis, share capital of CHF 100,000 divided into 100,000 bearer or registered shares of CHF 1.00 nominal value, board representation system and publication organ. The deed must be circulated and signed by each founder before notarisation; the notary will authenticate all signatures and issue a certified notarial exemplar for filing. File a capital payment certificate to be obtained from a Swiss bank after the paid-up capital is credited to a blocked account in the company's name.
required_dossiers: Draft deed of incorporation and articles of association
Notarisation instruction letter signed by each founder/director
Founders' photocopies of passports or Swiss identity cards
Certificate of non-identical company name/negative search from zug.ch/Handelsregisteramt
Bank certificate confirming the paid-up minimum capital deposit into a blocked nominative account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar or notary queries a deficiency (e.g., defective clauses, insufficient capital certificate), amend the instrument and re-submit with a supplementary notarial endorsement; a one-time re-notarisation within 30 days usually cures the defect without a new founding meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Share Capital and Issuance of Bank Blocking Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank licensed by FINMA and operating in Zug/Zurich (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank or a FINMA-licensed private bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a non-operating corporate share-capital account in the name to be registered, i.e., AI PET ROBOT AG. Transfer or deposit the minimum paid-up portion of CHF 50,000 (20% of the CHF 100,000 par value) from each founder in proportion to subscriptions. Hold funds in escrow/blocked status until the Commercial Register confirms the company is registered. Request the bank to issue a certificate of blocked capital confirming availability for the company. The bank releases the account automatically after registration receipt from the registry. If a guarantee is used for the unpaid portion, obtain a Swiss bank guarantee irrevocable in favour of the company and covering the full deficiency.
required_dossiers: Founding deed (draft certified copy)
Identification documents of authorized signatories and beneficial owners (AML/KYC)
Reservation of corporate name confirmation (name search certificate)
Bank account opening forms and source-of-funds declarations
Notarised instruction to block funds in the capital contribution account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced KYC due diligence or withholds the blocking certificate pending clarification, provide a concise capital-source declaration, corporate chart showing ultimate beneficial owners, and founding deed excerpt; the bank will then re-issue the certificate. If a bank refuses the account, select another licensed bank and re-initiate with complete notarised dossiers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the Commercial Register Application and Governance Declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug / Commercial Registry of the Canton of Zug; subsequent electronic publication in SHAB
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarisation, file the certified incorporation deed and supporting declarations through the Swiss Commercial Register electronic interface (www.zefix.ch / eGRIS or registered e-mail with digital signature accepted in Canton Zug). Include: incorporation application (Anmeldung), certified deed, capital deposit certificate or bank guarantee, appointment forms signed by directors, sample signatures, and an auditor designation statement (or declaration of opting-out if the company qualifies under Art. 727a CO). The registrar will validate that the company name complies with naming law, the registered office is in Zug, and the capital has been paid. Cause the registry to make the entry and issue the certified excerpt; upon entry, the company acquires legal personality.
required_dossiers: Certified notarial deed of incorporation and articles of association
Application form for entry in the Commercial Register (Handelsregister-Anmeldung)
Bank blocking certificate or bank guarantee for unpaid capital
Declarations of acceptance by board members; specimen signatures
Designation of the registered office representative (domicile representative), if applicable
Auditor appointment/opting-out declaration if permitted by law
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry files a deficiency notice, rectify within the statutory cure period (usually 30 days) by submitting amended documents or supplementary explanations through counsel/notary; unresolved defects lead to formal refusal, after which re-filing fees may be waived if the corrected application is entered within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration Organisation and Publication of SHAB Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB) and Cantonal Tax Office of Zug (for registration/withholding and VAT purposes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, verify the published SHAB excerpt and apply for the legal entity identification number (UID) automatically assigned to the firm. Hold the constitutive board meeting to approve issuance of share certificates, open the operating bank account, adopt the organisational regulations, and define the signature regime. Notify the Zug tax office of the registered office for corporate income tax, VAT and withholding tax purposes; apply where necessary for VAT number (MWST-Nr) if annual turnover exceeds CHF 100,000. Preserve the notarised deed, share certificates, and the certified commercial register excerpt in the registered office dossier.
required_dossiers: Certified commercial register excerpt
Board resolution/minutes of constitutive meeting
Share certificates and share register
Application forms for UID and VAT (MWST) registration (via ESTV/Geover and cantonal forms)
Mailing address and banking details for tax correspondence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UID/VAT application is returned for missing pending registration extract, resubmit with the final certified extract within 10 days; if share register deficiencies are identified by the tax office, correct with a subsequent notarial or board minute and re-submit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canton of Zug Department for Economic Affairs (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit) and the Swiss Federal Office of Communications (OFCOM) for radio and speech synthesis frequency aspects, together with SUVA as accident insurance supervisor; no separate national factory license applies to this product assembly activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Cantonal operating permit for assembly/manufacturing activity with low-emission final assembly (Betriebsbewilligung/Arbeitsbewilligung), together with an OFCOM conformity declaration for embedded short-range radio modules and commercial registration confirmation

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment FOEN (Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU), with enforcement delegated to the Canton of Zug Environmental Protection Office (Amt für Umweltschutz)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Simplified EIA-Notification category — no full EIR is required because the operation involves final assembly of robotic toys, no hazardous production processes, and no significant pollutant releases; however, an environmental self-declaration and waste-handling registration are required in Canton Zug.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Municipal wastewater discharge pH 6.5–9.5 and total organic carbon (TOC) discharge limit below 20 mg/L; VOC emissions from cleaning/lubricants below the federal threshold requiring a VOC-authorisation (typically <3% solvent content or annual use <150 kg of VOC; below this no licence needed); compliance with Swiss requirements on waste electrical and electronic equipment (OREA/VREG Ordinance on Returns, Take-Back and Disposal of Electrical and Electronic Equipment) for end-of-life robo-toys; lithium-ion batteries included with the robotic pet must be marked and recycled under Swiss Battery Ordinance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Zug Fire Prevention Inspectorate (Gebäudeversicherung des Kantons Zug, Feuerpolizei) for the assembly premises, including local fire extinguishing systems and emergency egress inspection; structural load compliance certificate confirming floor-load capacity for storage racks and assembly stations; occupational safety clearance from Suva (Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund) for the use of small hand-tools, chargers and battery testing stations, including a workplace hazard assessment, instruction records, and a valid accident insurance registration for all employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA) / Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung (ESTV), Administration fédérale des contributions (AFC), Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni (AFC); digital portal: 'My ESTV' at estv.admin.ch; public commercial register: Zefix at zefix.ch.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Swiss AG (Aktiengesellschaft) receives its permanent UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) automatically upon entry into the cantonal Commercial Register, which is the compulsory first registration step. The UID is the statutory business identifier used for VAT, direct tax, and statistical purposes. For a non-resident entity without a Swiss commercial-register seat, the ESTV assigns a UID and Swiss VAT account upon written/online application (Form 171 plus supporting statute, board resolution, and proof of foreign registration); the applicant not established in Switzerland must designate a Swiss service-of-process address and may be required to appoint a Swiss fiscal representative. All VAT accounts are administered centrally by the ESTV VAT division, while income-tax assessments are handled by canton Zurich or the relevant canton with federal corporate tax coordination via the Consensus/EWR system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation, Territorial_Scope (resident AG taxed on worldwide income; foreign permanent-establishment profits and foreign real estate exempt under Swiss territorial exemption); Tax_Exempt_Zone not applicable; no Pass_Through_Eligible classification for an AG.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections exist in Switzerland; the AG is a mandatory entity-level taxpayer. Available statutory elections: (1) Swiss VAT small-business election to opt out of VAT if turnover does not exceed CHF 250,000; (2) Swiss VAT group election (Steuergruppe) for related Swiss entities under a single UID; (3) participation-exemption election/waiver for qualifying dividends and capital gains; (4) patented IP-box election (90% income exemption) and R&D super-deduction (150%); (5) canton-level tax grouping (e.g., Zug, Schwyz) for cantonal direct taxes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT – Swiss Federal Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer MWST / TVA / IVA).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual taxable turnover for Swiss-established enterprises; CHF 250,000 threshold for the voluntary small-business exemption election; non-resident suppliers generally reverse-charged on Swiss B2B services, but must register for Swiss VAT if supplying e-services or goods to Swiss consumers and exceeding CHF 100,000 in annual Swiss-derived turnover. Interactive AI robotic toys sold B2C in Switzerland are subject to the 8.1% standard rate; no reduced rate applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no API-based fiscal stamping, and no continuous transaction control in Switzerland. Mandatory elements are the Swiss QR-Bill/QR-Rechnung payment standard for customer invoicing and statutory invoice content requirements under Art. 26 MWSTG. Electronic invoicing (EDI/Peppol/e-bill) is accepted, but fiscal returns must be filed electronically through the 'My ESTV' portal on a quarterly basis. For exporters, export declarations must pass through Swiss customs 'e-dec' or equivalent digital customs clearance systems.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export supply of goods qualifies for the Swiss 0% VAT rate under Art. 21-22 MWSTG only if (a) economic ownership of the goods is transferred to a non-Swiss buyer, (b) the goods are physically transported/consigned abroad, and (c) the seller obtains and retains sufficient documentary proof of export within the VAT return period applicable to the supply. Services directly related to the exported robotic goods or international transport/logistics services can also be zero-rated when the recipient is abroad and rights are effectively used outside Switzerland. Input VAT relating to the zero-rated export is fully creditable to the exporter.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhrdeklaration / e-dec export) with customs receipt stamp or electronic clearance certificate
Commercial transport evidence: Bill of Lading (Konossement), Air Waybill, CMR international consignment note, or postal/courier export certificate showing non-Swiss consignee and destination
Inward remittance certificate or bank statement evidencing receipt of export proceeds in CHF or convertible foreign currency (pipeline benchmark; Switzerland has no exchange-control requirement)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss Federal Tax Administration may retrospectively review export proof within the 10-year statutory books-and-records retention period. If 0% zero-rating is improperly claimed, the export VAT is reclaimed at 8.1% with default interest, and input VAT credits are clawed back. Administrative penalties under Arts. 96-98 MWSTG range up to three times the evaded tax, plus imprisonment in serious cases, and forged export documentation triggers Swiss Penal Code Art. 251 plus customs-evasion fines up to five times the evaded duties. For foreign entities, the ESTV may also deny refund entitlement and revoke the VAT registration for persistent false export zero-rating. The mandatory 180-day FX repatriation benchmark is a contractual/pipeline control, not a Swiss statutory requirement; failure to repatriate does not independently trigger Swiss VAT clawback but is treated as a red flag in audit scoring.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB; Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse / Banca nazionale svizzera), co-supervised for banking and financial market conduct by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc (CHF) is a fully convertible currency. Switzerland operates an open liberalised legal order with no exchange-control statute, no regime differentiated between current account and capital account transactions, and no approval requirement for inward remittance, dividend payment, loan repayment, or liquidation proceeds. Capital can be moved freely in or out of the country in any internationally traded currency. The only material frictions for profit remittance are tax-oriented, not exchange-control-oriented: dividends paid by the CH_AG to foreign shareholders attract a 35% Swiss anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer), which is reclaimable in full or substantially reduced under an applicable double tax treaty or where the beneficiary can invoke the LOB-consistent refund procedure. The CH_AG may hold foreign currency accounts (USD, EUR, CNY, etc.) without restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender rules, no repartriation deadline, and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts in Switzerland. The CH_AG is free to maintain export earnings in USD, EUR, or CNY, provided such amounts are properly reflected in the financial statements under the Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) and in VAT export evidence under the Swiss VAT Act. The SNB does not require or request any conversion of foreign export currencies into CHF.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (SIC clearing and payment distribution)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium. FINMA-supervised Swiss digital banking providers (e.g., Yuh, Neon, Zak by Bank Cler) can serve as agile operational accounts for daily disbursements and card rails. Offshore EU/UK electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Revolut Business, Wise Business, or Payoneer do not hold a Swiss banking licence and cannot access SIC direct clearing; they may be used only as auxiliary collection or disbursement channels with a licensed Swiss correspondent bank acting as the underlying clearing entity. The EU/EEA passporting regime does not extend to Switzerland, so a foreign EMI transacting into Swiss accounts must rely on structural co-operation agreements with FINMA-licensed institutions or obtain FINMA authorization under Swiss AML/PSA frameworks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is globally permitted in Switzerland: FINMA's recognized video and online identification procedures (based on the Anti-Money Laundering Act, AMLA, and FINMA anti-money laundering ordinances) allow verified digital identification without physical company attendance. In practice, Tier-1 Swiss banks retain discretion to request a physical or video interview with the board of directors when the AG is foreign-controlled, when beneficial owners are non-Swiss tax residents, or when the capital structure involves multi-tier offshore holding entities. A physical presence in Switzerland is not a mandatory legal requirement for opening an account, but it pragmatically expedites approval and reduces compliance friction for a CH_AG treasury.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) opacity through multi-tier foreign shareholding or intermediate holding entities without economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory share register (Aktienbuch); extract from the Swiss Commercial Register (Handelsregisterauszug); group org chart identifying all intermediate vehicles; signed beneficial ownership declaration per FINMA guidance; passport and address proof of all natural persons holding or controlling more than 25%; corporate registry extracts of all offshore intermediate entities; three years of source-of-funds evidence where relevant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection materially exceeding the minimum AG capital (CHF 100,000; at least 20% paid-in, minimum CHF 50,000) and insufficiently explained
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised capital increase resolution and shareholders' meeting minutes; bank statements of the transferring shareholder showing source of funds; shareholders' loan or subordination agreement (if part is considered debt); board-approved business plan with 24-month liquidity forecast; supplier framework agreements and logistics contracts demonstrating purpose of the funds; evidence of product stock availability and distribution contracts for the interactive AI pet robot line.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP screening hit on any foreign shareholder, director, or counterparty in the trading chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative screening reports against SECO, OFAC, EU, UN, and UK sanctions lists; PEP status disclosure forms; negative media and adverse-information verification; source-of-wealth statement; identification of publicly listed shareholders with a clear ultimate natural person chain; legal declaration from a Swiss law firm confirming no sanctioned party has control rights; remediation evidence in case of false-positive hits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border trade payment pattern inconsistent with the declared low-risk ISIC 3240 robotic toy manufacturing profile (e.g., high-value advances to Asian suppliers or round-trip disbursements)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Purchase orders, pro-forma invoices with Incoterms 2020, customs declarations and export/import documentation, warehouse and logistics provider certificates, inspection reports, landed-cost breakdowns, master distribution agreements, and VAT export evidence; each outbound wire must tie to a dated commercial contract evidencing the specific shipment milestone.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital should be wired to the dedicated Capital Escrow Account held at the chosen Tier-1 Swiss bank using an IBAN in CH format, cleared through SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) for CHF or EuroSIC for EUR. There is no Swiss statutory purpose-code schema; the wire reference should state 'Capital increase / Einlage Kapitalerhöhung' plus the notary file number and the AG registration number (UID). Verification by the receiving bank requires: (i) the notarised capital increase resolution, (ii) evidence of payment of at least the legally required portion of the new share capital (generally 20% or CHF 50,000), and (iii) the updated Commercial Register excerpt. Inbound BIBC/foreign-currency transfers for shareholder loans must be referenced separately as 'Shareholder loan / Aktionärsdarlehen' to allow the bank to distinguish equity from debt and avoid unintended tax or AML classification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for CH_AG treasury: (a) SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) for direct supplier payments up to approximately CHF 1 million per transaction; (b) Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP 600 (SWIFT MT700/MT707) for high-value component procurement, particularly for hardware and battery modules sourced from Asia, with sight or usance tenors; (c) SWIFT MT202/MT202 COV for bank-to-bank cover to the LC issuing bank or for correspondent clearing; (d) CHF domestic supplier and payroll payments via SIC ISO 20022 (pacs.008) and SIC5 instant payment; (e) EUR cross-border payments via TARGET2 or EuroSIC; (f) USD outbound via Fedwire/CHIPS through the Swiss bank's US correspondent network; (g) commercial card rails (Stripe, Visa/Mastercard) for B2C sales of the robotic companion products, with proceeds settled to the Swiss operational account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forward contracts (CHF/USD, CHF/EUR, CHF/CNY) with tenors standardised to 1, 3, 6, and 12 months under an FX master agreement (IFEMA or EMTA FXMM) with a Tier-1 Swiss counterparty
FX swaps (swap points on SIC/CLS delivery) for rolling management of net USD and EUR receivables from export sales
Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS) under ISDA 2002 with a Credit Support Annex (CSA) to convert long-term USD/EUR revenue exposure into CHF liquidity
OTC vanilla FX options (calls and puts) on CHF pairs under ISDA 1992/2002 or the 1998 FX-ISDA with collateral management
CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) against USD for hedging onshore RMB component sourcing, where the underlying trade invoice cannot be settled as a deliverable CNH forward

Exchange-traded futures and options on EUR/CHF or USD/CHF listed on Eurex as a collateral-efficient or cleared alternative, subject to board-approved treasury policy limits and formal FX risk management guidelines

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements, Directors' Report and (where applicable) auditor's report, submitted for approval and discharge at the Annual General Meeting (AGM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No filing to a regulatory agency for a non-listed small AG; the approved documents are retained at the registered office and must be produced to the Commercial Register (Handelsregisteramt) on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date under Art. 699 CO; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Shareholders may petition the court to convene the AGM; directors face civil liability; the Commercial Register may issue compliance orders and ultimately order official dissolution and strike-off under Art. 938b et seq. CO

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (federal direct tax, cantonal and communal profit taxes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Tax Administration of the Canton of Zug (Steuerverwaltung Zug), acting for the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) and the Zug communal tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the balance-sheet date; for a 31 December year-end the cantonal filing date is normally 30 June of the following year, with extension on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest (approx. 4.5% pa), procedural fines up to CHF 1,000 under federal law and corresponding cantonal penalties, assessment by estimation where no return is filed, enforced collection and bankruptcy proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Final VAT Return (definitive settlement of the VAT period; for calendar-year filers, the year is closed by the fourth-quarter return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / FTA), VAT Division, Berne
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the VAT settlement period; a calendar-year VAT period closes on 31 December, so the final annual return is due by 1 March of the following year (29 February in leap years)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest, procedural fines for late filing, VAT evasion penalties up to the tax amount involved, enforced distraint and criminal prosecution for wilful fraud

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Employer's Wage and Social Insurance Statement (AHV/IV/EO/ALV wage declaration) and contribution settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Compensation Office of Zug (Ausgleichskasse des Kantons Zug); electronic wage data transmitted to the Central Compensation Office (ZAS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January following the wage year (year-end closing and employee statements issued to staff by that date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Employer remains liable for unpaid AHV/IV/EO/ALV contributions plus default interest; administrative fines up to CHF 30,000 for wilful non-compliance and criminal prosecution for contribution evasion

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary statutory audit is mandatory where an AG exceeds at least two of the following thresholds in two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total CHF 20 million; annual turnover CHF 40 million; annual average of 250 full-time employees. Listed companies and certain regulated entities require ordinary audit regardless. A limited audit is required for other companies unless the AG averages fewer than 10 full-time employees and all shareholders unanimously waive auditing (opting-out).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957-967 CO), i.e. Swiss statutory GAAP; voluntarily SWISS GAAP FER; IFRS permitted for consolidated statutory accounts and mandatory where the parent company is listed

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland does not impose an annual UBO confirmation filing to a register. The AG must keep its share register current on each transfer and must report changes of legal and beneficial ownership in the annual tax return. Banks and AML-obliged persons collect UBO self-declarations; judicial, tax and supervisory authorities can compel disclosure of beneficial owners on request. No annual confirmation statement is due at the Commercial Register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800-4,500 per year for commercial registered-office, domiciliation and corporate-secretarial services in Zurich or Zug (approx. CHF 1,600-4,000)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,600-13,000 per year for a statutory limited audit of a small AG (approx. CHF 5,000-11,500); ordinary statutory audits of larger AGs range from USD 10,000-35,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined Swiss effective rate for the Zug jurisdiction (2024): 11.9% - Federal statutory CIT rate of 8.5% on after-tax profit (equivalent to 7.83% on pre-tax profit) plus Zug cantonal/communal profit tax of approximately 4.19% of pre-tax profit; national combined rate range 11.9% to 21.0% depending on canton and commune.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Zug Patent Box: 90% statutory exemption of qualifying patent and comparable IP income; R&D super-deduction: additional deduction of up to 50% of qualifying Swiss R&D personnel costs (up to 80% of external contract research); Notional Interest Deduction (Zug): deduction on excess hybrid-equity capital; participation exemption: 100% exemption of qualifying dividend and capital-gain income from substantial participations; transitional relief for old auxiliary statuses abolished from 2020.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Verified combined return: Canton of Zug 'Steuererklärung juristische Personen' (Tax Return for Legal Entities) with integrated Federal direct tax declaration (DBG); electronic filing via the Zug web portal 'Zug Tax Portal' (Steueramt Zug, E-Steuererklärung) and certified Swiss tax preparation software; a single submission simultaneously satisfies cantonal, communal and federal corporate income tax obligations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory deadline is six (6) months following the close of the financial year; applications for extension (up to a further 3 months) are generally granted in Zug; extended deadlines beyond 9 months require a valid reason and prior written application; interim tax payments (payables) are due quarterly based on prior-year assessments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered AG name, UID (Swiss company identification number), legal form and registered seat in Zug, date of incorporation in the cantonal commercial register, statutory purpose including ISIC 3240 manufacture of bionic companion robotic animals.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Install the Swiss AG as the tax-resident company; disclose all foreign permanent establishments, branch registrations and foreign sales channels; non-resident shareholders are not taxable on Swiss CIT but must be identifiable for treaty and withholding purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assets and liabilities as per Swiss Code of Obligations; share capital at par (minimum CHF 100,000 nominal, CHF 20,000 minimum paid-up in Zug standard AG); legal reserves, retained earnings and net profit/loss of the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transactions with non-resident shareholders, including loans, share premium and director's advances, must be shown at arm's-length amounts and fully documented to avoid hidden profit distribution recharacterization and 35% verrechnungssteuer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net profit in accordance with the income statement; R&D expenses, hardware component inventory movements, marketing/licensing costs and administrative expenses attributable to the AI pet robot line.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border sales of robotic units to foreign related distributors must be priced at arm's length under the Swiss TP rules; reductions or additions will be examined against the CUP method using independent distributor benchmarks.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses: fines, penalties, unjustified entertainment expenditure, hidden profit distributions to shareholders, professional tax advisor costs above business purpose, depreciation on non-business assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany royalties paid to a foreign IP-holding parent must be supported by patent registration, license agreements and value-chain documentation, otherwise they will be disallowed full add-back with potential 35% withholding tax characterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5: Federal and Cantonal Taxable Result
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of federal profit tax base (8.5% net) and Zug cantonal taxable profit; deduction line for patent box income, R&D super-deduction, participation income and any capital loss offsets within the seven-year carry-forward window.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an AG with non-resident investors, the board must minute the substance in Switzerland, including decision-making at Zug board meetings, so that profit attributable to Swiss management and IP remains taxable exclusively in Switzerland.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Zug capital tax assessed on qualified paid-in capital and reserves at the preferential Zug rate of 0.015% of taxable equity (0.0015% effective after deduction of the privileged capital base).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The capital tax computation is unaffected by non-resident ownership; foreign shareholders may not claim relief from capital tax and no treaty reduction applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge (Verspätungszuschlag) up to CHF 10,000 per filing instance, plus additional cantonal surcharges after formal reminders; negligent errors attract a penalty of up to one-third of the under-declared tax under DBG Art. 175; willful evasion is penalized up to three times the evaded tax under DBG Art. 174; untruthful or falsified documentation supporting the return converts the case to tax fraud (DBG Art. 186) with imprisonment up to two years or monetary penalty; default interest of 4.75% accrues on all late assessments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends distributed by a Swiss AG to shareholders, including non-resident shareholders; the tax is due to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA) before distribution and is normally withheld by the paying company from the gross dividend.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Step 1: Swiss company files the annual WHT return with the FTA and pays the 35% tax at source. Step 2: Non-resident shareholder applies for refund using FTA form 'Antrag um Rückerstattung der Verrechnungssteuer' (Application for Refund of the Withholding Tax), submitted within three years of the end of the calendar year of payment. Step 3: The applicant must attach a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its home-country tax authority; for US shareholders, IRS Form 6166; for EU shareholders, the standard EU residency certificate adopted under the Savings Tax Directive or DTA model; Step 4: The FTA verifies beneficial ownership and issues a refund of the difference between 35% and the applicable treaty rate (US-Switzerland DTA: 5% if the recipient holds at least 10% of the Swiss company's voting rights, 15% in other cases; Germany-Switzerland DTA: 10% for substantial participation, 15% otherwise); under the MLI Principal Purpose Test the treaty rate is lost where the shareholder structure lacks substance and was inserted principally for treaty shopping.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: no Swiss withholding tax is imposed on patent or technology royalties paid by a Swiss AG to a non-resident licensor (statutory 0%); interest paid by a Swiss AG on ordinary intercompany or bank debt financing also carries no Swiss withholding tax (0%); however, interest on publicly issued Swiss bonds, money market instruments and structured finance securities is subject to the 35% Verrechnungssteuer, with treaty refunds available to non-residents (typically 0% to 10% depending on the treaty); hidden interest distributions on shareholder loans exceeding arm's-length rates are recharacterized as dividends and attract the full 35% withholding tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Swiss Local File mandatory if annual group turnover equals or exceeds CHF 50 million; Master File mandatory if consolidated group turnover equals or exceeds CHF 1 billion; simplified contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is required even below the Local File threshold where related-party transactions exceed: CHF 5 million for purchase/sale of goods, CHF 1 million for services (including management fees and R&D cost-sharing), and CHF 0.5 million for financial transactions or IP licensing; the Swiss tax administration may compel documentation for any taxpayer by formal assessment notice under Art. 21 of the Tax Administration Act of 2020.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: OECD Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) for zero-tax jurisdictions are not applicable to Switzerland, which levies statutory corporate tax at an effective rate above 11%; nevertheless, the Swiss AG must demonstrate genuine commercial substance for treaty and intra-group purposes: local board meetings in Zug, decision-making bodies present in Switzerland, local employees with technical competence for the AI pet robot product, and a real office premises; artificial arrangements diverting profit to a zero-tax foreign entity and leaving the Swiss AG as a bare shell will fail the Swiss anti-abuse doctrine (substance-over-form), the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test for treaty benefits, and the beneficial owner requirement under the withholding tax refund procedure; the Federal Supreme Court and the FTA will reattribute the profit and deny treaty protection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underreporting worldwide taxable profit, omitting foreign bank accounts or Stripe payment-rail revenue of the AI pet robot business, falsifying inventory records, or using fabricated purchase invoices to reduce Swiss profits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty assessment under DBG Art. 174 (federal), StHG Art. 55/56 (cantonal Zug), and Art. 186 (serious tax fraud) for use of forged or falsified documents; fine of up to three times the evaded tax plus default interest at 4.75% per year; in tax-fraud cases imprisonment up to two years or monetary penalty; statute of limitation for gross negligence is 10 years; all group tax benefits including patent box and foreign tax credits are revoked retroactively.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Chairman, CFO and any board member signing the tax return are personally subject to criminal fines and imprisonment for tax fraud; known officers may be named in the penalty order even after the company's solvency; the FTA may issue a travel ban (exit restriction) and international debt-collection assistance to enforce collection against personal assets where the director is deemed the 'wirtschaftlich Beteiligter'.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Non-Compliance and Shell Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to non-resident shareholders without deducting the Swiss verrechnungssteuer of 35%, or using a foreign nominee/holding company lacking economic substance to claim treaty-refund of 35% back to a 0% jurisdiction; stripping profits via a documented 'letterbox' Zug company with no personnel or management, while the entire board meets abroad
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Swiss paying company becomes personally liable for payment of the entire 35% withholding tax together with interest (Art. 11 VStG) and a fine up to three times the endangered tax pursuant to Art. 66 VStG; treaty refund denied and taxable dividend reclassified, with potential criminal proceedings for tax fraud against the responsible directors and the Swiss agent of any foreign shell entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the Swiss authorized signatory (manager) are jointly and severally liable for withholding tax debts of the company upon insolvency; under Art. 12 SchKG (Debt Enforcement Act), officers who knowingly caused tax shortfalls by failing to remit withheld sums face personal liability and debt-enforcement seizure of their Swiss bank accounts; criminal conviction may carry imprisonment or fines payable from the director's personal estate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering, UBO Transparency and FATCA/CRS Reporting Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Swiss AG as a conduit for crypto-currency assets held by an anonymous foreign beneficial owner, failing to maintain know-your-beneficial-owner records of the non-resident shareholder, misreporting the AG's US-shareholder status under FATCA/CRS, or transacting with sanctioned persons via the Stripe/credit-card payment rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG/AMLA) by financial intermediaries involved, FINMA enforcement orders, penalty fines up to CHF 1 million; Swiss Code of Obligations disclosure violations attracting fines and delisting/withdrawal of business license; FATCA/CRS misreporting penalty of up to CHF 250,000 per infraction plus corrective administrative proceedings; the tax authority may reverse all legal non-recognition of the AG, treating it as transactionally opaque.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the AMLA and the Swiss Criminal Code, directors who knowingly conduct suspect transactions or fail to report them face imprisonment up to five years and personal monetary fines; the corporate veil is pierced when shareholders and directors use the AG to defraud creditors or tax authorities, permitting civil restitution proceedings in the Swiss Federal Criminal Court; board members are prohibited from leaving Switzerland pending investigation and may be subjected to asset freezes and travel bans.
